detail.body:
## Overview

AITER `biased_grouped_topk` runs an LDS group scan even when the grouping cannot eliminate any expert — that is, when `topk_group >= num_expert_group`, so every group is selected. This adds a register-resident Triton sigmoid+bias top-k and substitutes it at `rocm_aiter_ops.biased_grouped_topk`, the single call site both ROCm routers reach.

Previously this PR specialised `rocm_aiter_grouped_topk` only. Moving it to the wrapper came out of review (thanks @simondanielsson) and covers both paths without touching routing metadata:

| caller | group arguments it passes |
|---|---|
| `GroupedTopKRouter` | the model's own `1/1` for a degenerate router |
| `FusedTopKBiasRouter` | a count synthesised to fit an AITER kernel — measured `2/2` for a 64-expert router — with `topk_group == num_expert_group` |

`vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/experts/rocm_aiter_moe.py` is no longer modified; the diff is three files, additions only.

## Claims

- 1.67×–2.15× on the routing op on gfx942, and 1.16×–1.57× per shape on gfx950, under CUDA graph replay, across the configurations listed below.
- The gate stops at 512 experts and top-8. On gfx950 the kernel loses at top-16 (896-expert top-16 down to 0.62×), so those routers keep AITER — see *Scope and bounds*.
- Equivalent to the call it replaces whenever no group is eliminated, including `num_expert_group == topk_group > 1`, which is the shape `FusedTopKBiasRouter` produces.
- Eager execution is **not** faster, so it is excluded by the substitution rather than claimed as a win.
- Selected expert ids match AITER on 3323 of 3328 routing calls in a live Moonlight-16B-A3B forward and on 1248 of 1248 in Kimi-VL-A3B.
- **Scope: single-token batches only (`_MAX_TOKENS = 1`), as suggested in review**, i.e. one request decoding without speculation, which is where the end-to-end gain is. Larger batches keep AITER.
- End to end on MI355X with current `main`, five models with 64 to 384 experts, 1k to 32k context: **single-request decode is 0.4% to 4.2% faster on every model**, and higher concurrency is within noise; nothing regresses beyond the same-arm drift. GSM8K is unchanged on GLM-5.3-Flash and Kimi-K2.6. Earlier gfx942 runs were within noise.
- No new env var, and no change to router selection or to the advertised routing method.

## Dispatch scope: why this is restricted to CUDA graph steps

The kernel's advantage is device time. Timed from a plain Python loop it is *slower* — it is a Triton launch from Python against a single C++ dispatch, and that overhead is not amortised.

Because the gate is a token-count bound rather than an execution-phase check, eager steps can reach it, so this was measured end to end with `--enforce-eager`, interleaved B-A-B-A on Moonlight:

| in / out | concurrency | AITER tok/s | ungated PR tok/s | Δ | same-arm drift |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| 64 / 256 | 8 | 488.7 | 471.8 | **−3.5%** | 0.6% / 1.2% |
| 64 / 256 | 32 | 1910.4 | 1876.9 | **−1.8%** | 0.8% / 0.1% |
| 1024 / 1024 | 8 | 780.8 | 758.1 | **−2.9%** | 0.8% / 0.2% |
| 1024 / 1024 | 32 | 3008.8 | 2915.3 | **−3.1%** | 0.0% / 0.9% |

Consistent sign and a magnitude several times the drift, so this is a real regression, not noise. The dispatch therefore substitutes only while a CUDA graph is being captured, tested with `torch.cuda.is_current_stream_capturing()` as `custom_all_reduce.py` and `sparse_attn_indexer.py` already do, and eager steps keep AITER. An earlier revision tested `get_forward_context().cudagraph_runtime_mode` instead; that misses every FULL graph under the V2 model runner, which captures them with the forward context set to `NONE` (`vllm/v1/worker/gpu/cudagraph_utils.py`), so on current main it substituted only inside PIECEWISE graphs. Re-running the same eager A/B with the check in place:

| in / out | concurrency | AITER tok/s | this PR tok/s | Δ | same-arm drift |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| 64 / 256 | 8 | 490.2 | 492.5 | +0.5% | 0.7% / 0.1% |
| 64 / 256 | 32 | 1934.9 | 1933.3 | −0.1% | 1.2% / 0.0% |
| 1024 / 1024 | 8 | 787.1 | 786.8 | −0.0% | 0.1% / 1.0% |
| 1024 / 1024 | 32 | 3018.7 | 3009.5 | −0.3% | 1.9% / 0.8% |

Instrumentation observed no Triton dispatches with `enforce_eager=True`. With graphs enabled, on current main and MI355X, a server records these substitution decisions while it captures its graphs:

| model | cudagraph mode | substituted with the forward-context check | substituted with the stream-capture check |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| Kimi-Linear-48B-A3B | `FULL_DECODE_ONLY` (forced by the model) | 0 of 2912 | 494 of 2912 |
| Moonlight-16B-A3B | `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` | 988 of 8190 | 1482 of 8190 |

494 is 19 captured decode sizes up to 128 tokens times 26 MoE layers; the remaining decisions are larger captured sizes, the profiling run and warm-up runs, all of which keep AITER. Those counts are with the earlier `_MAX_TOKENS = 128`; with the current `_MAX_TOKENS = 1` a Moonlight server substitutes 78 of 8190 decisions, all of them in the 1-token graphs, and keeps AITER everywhere else.

## Validation

All runs on one MI300X (gfx942, 304 CUs), torch 2.10.0, triton 3.6.0.

Three checkpoints are used, all with `num_expert_group=1`, `topk_group=1`, a sigmoid router and a `noaux_tc` correction bias. Which one carries which measurement, since they differ:

| model | experts / top-k | context | used for |
|---|---|---|---|
| Moonlight-16B-A3B | 64 / 6 | 8192 | routing comparison, e2e ≤6k, NIAH 4096, GPQA |
| Kimi-VL-A3B-Instruct | 64 / 6 | 131072 | routing comparison, e2e 1k |
| Kimi-Linear-48B-A3B | **256 / 8** | 1M | e2e 1k, GPQA, and the 8k/64k attempt |

NIAH ran at 4096 and GPQA at roughly 1k prompts, both well under the 8192 input length at which the engine fault described below appears, so those results and that fault are not in conflict.

Which model carries which measurement, since they differ:

| measurement | model | context used |
|---|---|---|
| unit, micro | — (kernel in isolation) | n/a |
| routing comparison | Moonlight-16B-A3B **and** Kimi-VL-A3B | short decode rows |
| e2e 1k/1k, 6k/1k | Moonlight-16B-A3B | ≤ 7k |
| e2e 1k/1k | Kimi-VL-A3B | ≤ 2k |
| e2e 8k/1k, 64k/1k | **not obtained** — see below | — |
| NIAH | Moonlight-16B-A3B | 4096 |
| GPQA | Moonlight-16B-A3B | ~1k prompts |

NIAH and GPQA ran on Moonlight at 4096 and ~1k respectively, both well under the 8192 input length at which the engine crash below appears, so there is no contradiction between those results and that crash.

### Unit

Against upstream `db3b0f0fa`:

```bash
pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_rocm_aiter_topk.py -k "flat_topk or substitutes"
# 61 passed on MI355X (gfx950), this PR at 7c6559d9 cherry-picked onto main 3966924d
```

Each correctness test compares against `rocm_aiter_ops.biased_grouped_topk(..., 1, 1, ...)` — the exact call being replaced — through the same wrapper production uses.

| test | coverage |
|---|---|
| `test_flat_topk_matches_aiter` | 40 cases: {bf16, fp32} × {renorm on, off} × 10 shapes, including primes/odd sizes that exercise the masked tail of `BLOCK_E = next_power_of_2(num_experts)`: `(3,257,8)`, `(7,131,5)`, `(13,509,7)`, `(1,2,1)`, `(5,65,3)` |
| `test_flat_topk_casts_bias_like_aiter` | bf16 gating with an fp32 bias — see *Bias dtype* |
| `test_flat_topk_matches_aiter_with_uneliminating_groups` | `num_expert_group == topk_group` ∈ {1, 2, 4, 8} × renorm on/off — the `FusedTopKBiasRouter` shape |
| `test_flat_topk_honours_routed_scaling` | `routed_scaling_factor` 1.0 / 2.446 / 2.827 |
| `test_biased_grouped_topk_substitutes_only_when_expected` | captures a real CUDA graph around the wrapper: it substitutes for `1/1` and `2/2` during capture, and not for `8/4` or in eager |

The rest of that file reports 34 failures in my container which reproduce identically on unmodified `db3b0f0fa` (34 failed / 5 passed before this change, 34 failed / 77 passed after it, measured before the review trim); this PR does not touch them.

```bash
pre-commit run --files vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/experts/rocm_aiter_moe.py \

  tests/kernels/moe/test_rocm_aiter_topk.py
```

### Micro

Per-call **device** time under CUDA graph replay, 50 calls captured per graph so the replay overhead is amortised ~50× instead of landing on both arms.

| gating | experts | tokens | AITER (µs) | PR (µs) | speedup |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| bf16 | 256 | 1 / 8 / 32 / 128 | 5.47 / 5.67 / 5.72 / 5.76 | 3.00 / 3.18 / 3.20 / 3.27 | 1.82× / 1.78× / 1.79× / 1.76× |
| bf16 | 384 | 1 / 8 / 32 / 128 | 6.80 / 7.03 / 7.07 / 7.14 | 4.01 / 4.14 / 4.16 / 4.26 | 1.69× / 1.70× / 1.70× / 1.67× |
| fp32 | 256 | 1 / 8 / 32 / 128 | 6.05 / 6.12 / 6.24 / 6.26 | 2.82 / 2.99 / 3.00 / 3.16 | 2.15× / 2.05× / 2.08× / 1.98× |
| fp32 | 384 | 1 / 8 / 32 / 128 | 7.33 / 7.54 / 7.61 / 7.62 | 3.56 / 3.70 / 3.73 / 3.79 | 2.06× / 2.04× / 2.04× / 2.01× |

That is gfx942 (MI300X) at 256 and 384 experts.

On gfx950 (MI355X), the same method over a wider range of shapes: bf16 gating, fp32 bias, `routed_scaling_factor` 2.446, renormalised, six random seeds per point, plus one input where a single row has an exactly tied top score. Expert ids matched a stable-sort reference on every input, and AITER's id set on all 192 random inputs.

| experts | top-k | AITER µs, 1 / 8 / 32 / 128 tokens | PR µs, 1 / 8 / 32 / 128 tokens | mean speedup | worst random launch | one tied row |
|---:|---:|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 64 | 6 | 5.40 / 5.79 / 5.85 / 5.77 | 3.45 / 3.65 / 3.72 / 3.74 | 1.57× | 1.51× | 1.33× |
| 256 | 8 | 5.21 / 5.35 / 5.46 / 5.51 | 3.99 / 4.27 / 4.26 / 4.45 | 1.27× | 1.06× | 1.06× |
| 384 | 8 | 5.36 / 5.88 / 5.93 / 5.97 | 4.62 / 5.12 / 5.12 / 5.13 | 1.16× | 1.13× | 0.92× |
| 512 | 8 | 5.50 / 6.11 / 6.17 / 6.23 | 4.56 / 5.20 / 5.20 / 5.45 | 1.18× | 0.98× | 0.95× |
| 512 | 16 | 6.59 / 7.11 / 7.17 / 7.24 | 5.36 / 5.85 / 5.92 / 6.97 | 1.18× | 0.80× | 0.78× |
| 768 | 16 | 11.36 / 12.37 / 12.42 / 12.45 | 6.75 / 7.26 / 7.29 / 8.06 | 1.67× | 1.04× | 0.98× |
| 896 | 16 | 6.97 / 7.66 / 7.72 / 7.75 | 6.79 / 7.26 / 7.29 / 8.07 | 1.03× | 0.65× | 0.62× |
| 1024 | 16 | 7.12 / 7.80 / 7.85 / 7.91 | 6.76 / 7.24 / 7.28 / 7.28 | 1.07× | 1.04× | 0.64× |

The advantage shrinks as the router widens on gfx950; it does not grow. The slow launches are the tie fallback: when a row has two experts with exactly equal biased scores among its top-k, the fast path picks more than k and that row redoes the selection, and the launch waits for its slowest row. bf16 logits make exact ties common enough at top-16 to matter (0.8% of rows at 896 experts, so about one 32-row launch in five), which is where the 0.6× launches come from. Rows above 512 experts or top-8 therefore stay on AITER.

### Routing comparison on live models

Comparing generated text between arms is not a usable instrument on this setup: it is not deterministic run to run — two baseline-only runs of the same four greedy prompts already diverge. Instead both kernels were run on identical inputs inside a live forward, AITER into the real buffers and the new kernel into scratch, with generation continuing on the AITER result so the measurement cannot perturb the run.

| model | calls compared | calls where **all** selected ids match | max abs weight delta |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Moonlight-16B-A3B | 3328 | 3323 | 4.77e-07 |
| Kimi-VL-A3B-Instruct | 1248 | 1248 | 4.77e-07 |

Both have `n_group=1`, `topk_group=1`, `scoring_func="sigmoid"`, `noaux_tc`, `norm_topk_prob=true`, 64 experts, top-6. The five differing Moonlight calls each carry a weight delta of 1.19e-07 or 4.77e-07; that is consistent with a near-tie in the biased score resolving to a different expert, but the weight delta alone does not prove the scores were exactly equal.

### End to end on MI300X (gfx942)

`vllm serve` + `vllm bench serve`, interleaved, one fresh server per block.

An initial sequential A/B (all of arm 0, then all of arm 1) showed +16–24% throughput. That did not reproduce under interleaved testing and has been withdrawn — the same AITER baseline measured 1789 tok/s sequentially and 2250 tok/s interleaved on a shared host.

| model | in / out | concurrency | Δ throughput | Δ TPOT | same-arm drift |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| Moonlight | 1024 / 1024 | 8 | +0.7% | −0.8% | 0.4% / 1.4% |
| Moonlight | 1024 / 1024 | 32 | +0.8% | −0.9% | 1.1% / 0.6% |
| Kimi-VL | 1024 / 1024 | 8 | +0.4% | −0.6% | 1.0% / 0.9% |
| Kimi-VL | 1024 / 1024 | 32 | +0.7% | −0.9% | 3.6% / 0.7% |
| Kimi-Linear | 1024 / 1024 | 8 | +1.1% | −1.1% | 0.4% / 0.4% |
| Kimi-Linear | 1024 / 1024 | 32 | +0.1% | −0.1% | 1.1% / 0.7% |

Comparable to the same-arm variation, so no gfx942 end-to-end speedup is claimed. The Kimi-Linear rows discard the first repetition of each block: the very first benchmark run of the campaign returned 1066 tok/s against 1510-1543 for the other seven runs of that point, a warm-up artefact rather than a property of either arm.

**The 8k/1k and 64k/1k points are now measured.** The earlier report that they could not be served was wrong, and the reason is worth stating because it is a bug in the benchmark harness rather than in serving.

`vllm bench serve --dataset-name random` samples token ids from `tokenizer.vocab_size`. For this checkpoint that is **163842**, while the model's embedding has `config.vocab_size` = **163840** rows, so ids 163840 and 163841 index past the table and the embedding gather faults. The dataset emits a *contiguous run* of ids, so a 65536-token prompt covers 40% of the vocabulary and nearly always includes one of the two; an 8192-token prompt covers 5%, which is why 8k completed under some seeds and not others. On stock vLLM, with no part of this PR installed, the identical 8192 configuration completes 3/3 with `--seed 7` and faults 3/3 with `--seed 1234`:

| seed | completed | `Memory access fault` |
|---|---|---|
| 7 | 8, 8, 8 | 0 |
| 1234 | 0, 0, 0 | 1 |

That also explains the fault seen earlier on a different machine with Kimi-VL, where the kernel named in the HSA exception was `at::native::vectorized_gather_kernel` — the embedding gather.

Replacing the synthesised prompts with real text (a custom dataset whose maximum token id is 138177, verified below the embedding size) removes the fault entirely: 8 of 8 runs complete at 64k with zero faults.

| in / out | concurrency | AITER tok/s | this PR tok/s | Δ throughput | Δ TPOT | same-arm drift |

| 8192 / 1024 | 4 | 4305.4 | 4466.3 | +3.7% | −4.0% | 4.1% / 1.7% |
| 8192 / 1024 | 8 | 6154.7 | 6162.5 | +0.1% | −1.2% | 1.4% / 1.8% |
| 65536 / 1024 | 1 | 13528.3 | 14305.7 | +5.7% | −7.0% | 8.6% / 8.4% |
| 65536 / 1024 | 2 | 18045.6 | 17927.5 | −0.7% | −1.6% | 1.7% / 0.9% |

Every point has a same-arm drift of the same size as the difference between arms, so these do not change the gfx942 conclusion. The 64k rows carry only 2 and 4 requests per run, which is why their drift is the largest in the table.

Every model below has a sigmoid router with a `noaux_tc` correction bias whose grouping eliminates nothing, so it reaches the substitution; the probe column is how many of the routing decisions a server makes while capturing its graphs took the Triton path (the rest are larger captured sizes, the profiling run and warm-up, which keep AITER).

MiniMax-M3.1-Flash routes through a group count `FusedTopKBiasRouter` synthesises (128 experts, top-4, 4/4); at that shape the kernel selects the same experts as AITER on all 17040 rows of a randomised check (fp32 and bf16 gating and bias, 1-128 rows), max weight difference 7.45e-08.

An earlier A/B on Kimi-Linear, taken before the graph-capture fix, measured +0.07% to +0.16%; the probe shows that run never substituted, so it is not used.

### Accuracy on MI300X (gfx942)

A/B on Moonlight through the served endpoint, lm-eval 0.4.13.

**NIAH** (RULER, 4096): the three reported task scores match between arms — `niah_multikey_1` 1.00/1.00, `niah_single_2` 0.94/0.94, `niah_single_1` 0.00/0.00. The subtask scoring zero on both arms is inconclusive; this is task-level agreement, not per-sample output agreement.

**GPQA** (`gpqa_diamond_zeroshot`, 198 questions, loglikelihood). A first single-run A/B looked like +2.0 points for this PR. Three interleaved runs per arm show the difference changes sign:

| run | AITER | this PR |
|---|---:|---:|
| 1 | 0.3131 | 0.3333 |
| 2 | 0.3384 | 0.3182 |
| 3 | 0.3485 | 0.3283 |

AITER alone spans 0.3131–0.3485 across its own three runs.

Repeated on Kimi-Linear-48B-A3B, three interleaved runs per arm:

| run | AITER | this PR |
|---|---:|---:|
| 1 | 0.3889 | 0.4040 |
| 2 | 0.3990 | 0.4192 |
| 3 | 0.3990 | 0.4091 |
| median | 0.3990 | 0.4091 |

Here this PR is nominally higher in all three runs, by 1.0 point. **That is not claimed as an accuracy improvement**: 1.0 point is 2 questions out of 198, well inside the ±3.4 point standard error, and a routing difference confined to 0.15% of calls has no mechanism by which it could make a model more accurate. Taken with the Moonlight runs, these results show no regression, but are not sufficient to establish accuracy equivalence.

### Bias dtype

`rocm_aiter_ops.biased_grouped_topk` casts `correction_bias` to the gating dtype before dispatching, because AITER raises on a mismatch. A bf16 gating output next to an fp32 correction bias is a common router layout, so without the same cast the new path would score experts at a precision the replaced path never uses, and could select different experts. `sigmoid_bias_flat_topk` therefore makes the same cast at its own entry; Removing the cast fails 4 of the 6 cases in `test_flat_topk_casts_bias_like_aiter`; the other two shapes happen not to be sensitive to the bias precision.

### Known behavioural differences

| input | result |
|---|---|
| well-formed gating | weights agree to 2e-3 in unit tests; selected ids match on 4571 of 4576 live routing calls across two models |
| near-ties in the biased score | weights agree to 1.19e-07; the index chosen among near-equal experts may differ |
| NaN in gating output | **materially different from AITER** (6/10 synthetic configs, max weight delta 0.93) |

If maintainers would rather the gate reject non-finite input, that is a small addition to `can_use_sigmoid_bias_flat_topk`.

## Details

### Why the substitution sits at the wrapper

Review asked whether a model with no grouping should simply not be routed to `GroupedTopKRouter`. Two things make the wrapper the better place.

First, the advertised routing method is not a label. `layer.py:378` takes it from `router.kernel_routing_method_type` and stores it on the MoE config, where the AITER mxfp4 expert kernels consume it: `_supports_routing_method` lists `[Renormalize, RenormalizeNaive, DeepseekV4, DeepSeekV3]`, `self.renormalize` is derived from the same tuple, and the apply path branches on `DeepSeekV3` to pick `score_mode="sigmoid"`. `MiniMax2` is in none of them, so degenerating `num_expert_group` 1 → None would make those backends refuse these models and would flip `renormalize` to False for a checkpoint whose config says `norm_topk_prob: true`.

Second, and more decisively, changing the router would not remove the op. Calling `fused_topk_bias` directly — the routine `FusedTopKBiasRouter` uses — with a 64-expert, top-6 sigmoid+bias router on ROCm with AITER enabled:

```
synthesised group count for 64 experts: 2
biased_grouped_topk CALLED 1x with (num_expert_group, topk_group) = (2, 2)
```

`_aiter_get_num_expert_group` picks a divisor AITER has a kernel for, with `topk_group == num_expert_group` so the grouping is a no-op. A model moved off `GroupedTopKRouter` would still reach the grouped kernel, with a fabricated two-group configuration in place of its real single group.

Specialising at `rocm_aiter_ops.biased_grouped_topk` covers both callers, needs no routing-metadata change, and generalises the condition from "one group" to "no group is eliminated".

### Relation to #49870

[#49870](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/49870) short-circuits the same degenerate shape for the case where AITER fused MoE is **not** enabled, which this PR does not touch.

### Scope and bounds

`can_use_sigmoid_bias_flat_topk` requires `topk_group >= num_expert_group`, a contiguous bias of exactly `num_experts`, and bounded token/expert/topk counts. The scoring function is not checked: at this call site the op is AITER's biased (sigmoid) top-k by construction, so matching that op is the contract. `_MAX_EXPERTS = 512` and `_MAX_TOPK = 8` are where the gfx950 measurements above stop showing a win: up to there the mean per shape is 1.16×–1.57× and no launch falls below 0.92×, even with a forced tie; at top-16 single tied rows pull launches to 0.62×–0.78×. An earlier revision of this PR accepted up to 1024 experts and top-32, set to cover the widest router in this family without having measured it there; the gfx950 sweep showed that was wrong, and those routers, Kimi-K3 (896 / top-16) among them, now keep AITER. `_MAX_TOKENS = 1` restricts it to single-token batches, one request decoding without speculation, where the end-to-end sweep shows a gain on every model; at larger batches the gain was within noise, so those keep AITER.

### Limitations

- Micro and unit tests on gfx942 and gfx950. The MI355X e2e and GSM8K runs are on current `main`; the gfx942 e2e, NIAH and GPQA runs are on an older build, see the next point.
- The e2e and accuracy comparisons used the container's own older vLLM build for both arms, because today's `main` cannot start against this image's AITER (`aiter.ops.flydsl.moe_common` missing, `fused_moe()` without `swiglu_limit`). Both arms are that same build differing only in this kernel. Unit and micro results are against `db3b0f0fa`.

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""Register-resident sigmoid + bias top-k for degenerate grouped routing.
+
+Several DeepSeek-V3-architecture checkpoints route with ``use_grouped_topk=True``
+but ``num_expert_group=1`` and ``topk_group=1``, so the group stage selects
+nothing: Moonlight-16B-A3B (64 experts, top-6) and Kimi-K2 (384 experts, top-8),
+both ``scoring_func="sigmoid"`` with a ``noaux_tc`` correction bias.  On ROCm this
+lands in ``aiter.biased_grouped_topk_hip`` (``grouped_topk_kernel<...,
+NUM_GRP=1>``), which keeps the biased scores in LDS and runs one serial round
+per selected expert of ``LDS scan -> shuffle argmax -> LDS invalidate -> LDS
+read of the pre-bias sigmoid``.
+
+With a single group the group-selection stage is the identity, so the op is
+exactly "sigmoid(logits) + bias -> top-k -> weights = sigmoid at the chosen
+experts (optionally renormalised, times routed_scaling_factor)".  This kernel
+does that with all scores held in registers: each score is packed with its
+expert index into a unique, order-preserving int64 key, so every round is a
+single ``tl.max`` plus an equality invalidate (no argmax pair reduction, no
+LDS round trips, ties broken towards the lower expert id).
+"""
+
+import torch
+
+from vllm.triton_utils import tl, triton
+
+# Shape bounds, not model bounds: no checkpoint is assumed. _MAX_TOKENS limits
+# this to single-token batches, i.e. one request decoding without speculation.
+# That is where it shows end to end (+0.4% to +4.2% output throughput across
+# five models on MI355X); at larger batches the router is a smaller share of
+# the step and the gain is within noise, so those keep AITER.
+# _MAX_EXPERTS and _MAX_TOPK are where this kernel stops beating AITER on
+# MI355X (gfx950), measured under CUDA graph replay with bf16 router logits:
+# up to 512 experts and top-8 it averages 1.16-1.57x per shape, and no launch
+# falls below 0.92x even with a forced score tie. At top-16 one row with an
+# exactly tied score sends the launch through the fallback path at 0.62-0.78x
+# (512, 896 and 1024 experts), and from 896 experts tie-free launches gain at
+# most 1.09x, so those routers keep AITER.
+_MAX_TOKENS = 1
+_MAX_EXPERTS = 512
+_MAX_TOPK = 8
+# One wave per token: every round's max is a pure in-wave reduction (no LDS
+# round trip / barrier), which is what bounds latency at decode batch sizes.
+_NUM_WARPS = 1
+
+
+@triton.jit
+def _sigmoid_bias_flat_topk_kernel(
+    logits_ptr,
+    bias_ptr,
+    topk_weights_ptr,
+    topk_ids_ptr,
+    stride_lm,
+    stride_wm,
+    stride_im,
+    routed_scaling_factor,
+    E: tl.constexpr,
+    BLOCK_E: tl.constexpr,
+    TOPK: tl.constexpr,
+    BLOCK_K: tl.constexpr,
+    RENORM: tl.constexpr,
+):
+    pid = tl.program_id(0)
+    offs = tl.arange(0, BLOCK_E)
+    emask = offs < E
+    row = logits_ptr + pid.to(tl.int64) * stride_lm
+
+    x = tl.load(row + offs, mask=emask, other=0.0).to(tl.float32)
+    b = tl.load(bias_ptr + offs, mask=emask, other=0.0).to(tl.float32)
+    # Same formula as the AITER kernel: 1 / (1 + 2^(-x * log2(e))).
+    s = 1.0 / (1.0 + tl.exp2(x * -1.4426950408889634))
+    # NaN logits (e.g. padded CUDA-graph rows) must not win selection: like
+    # AITER's '>'-based scan, treat them as score 0.
+    s = tl.where(s == s, s, 0.0)
+    sc = s + b
+
+    w_row = topk_weights_ptr + pid.to(tl.int64) * stride_wm
+    i_row = topk_ids_ptr + pid.to(tl.int64) * stride_im
+
+    # Fast path: TOPK rounds of fp32 max (DPP-fused v_max) that also record the
+    # round in which each expert was taken. With no exact score ties exactly
+    # TOPK experts are taken, round k == output slot k (descending, as AITER),
+    # and the weights come straight from registers.
+    v = tl.where(emask, sc, float("-inf"))
+    rnd = tl.full([BLOCK_E], -1, tl.int32)
+    for k in tl.static_range(TOPK):
+        m = tl.max(v, axis=0)
+        hit = v == m
+        rnd = tl.where(hit, k, rnd)
+        v = tl.where(hit, float("-inf"), v)
+    picked = rnd >= 0
+    n_picked = tl.sum(picked.to(tl.int32), axis=0)
+
+    if n_picked == TOPK:
+        if RENORM:
+            wsum = tl.sum(tl.where(picked, s, 0.0), axis=0)
+            scale = routed_scaling_factor / tl.maximum(wsum, 1e-20)
+        else:
+            scale = routed_scaling_factor
+        tl.store(w_row + rnd, s * scale, mask=picked)
+        tl.store(i_row + rnd, offs, mask=picked)
+    else:
+        # Exact ties: pack (order-preserving score, E-1-idx) into a unique
+        # int64 key so equal scores resolve to the lower expert id.
+        bits = sc.to(tl.int32, bitcast=True)
+        okey = bits ^ ((bits >> 31) & 0x7FFFFFFF)
+        key = (okey.to(tl.int64) << 32) | (BLOCK_E - 1 - offs).to(tl.int64)
+        sentinel = tl.full([BLOCK_E], -2147483648, tl.int32).to(tl.int64) << 32

At top-16 the kernel can lose to AITER. With bf16 logits a row occasionally has two experts with exactly equal biased scores inside its top-k; the fast path then picks more than k, that row redoes the selection, and the launch waits for it. At 896 experts / top-16 that is 0.8% of rows, so about one 32-row launch in five, and those launches run at 0.62x of AITER; 512/16 and 1024/16 behave the same way (0.78x and 0.64x). Up to 512 experts and top-8 the kernel averages 1.16x-1.57x per shape and no launch drops below 0.92x, even with a forced tie. So Kimi-K3 (896 / top-16) now keeps AITER. Thanks @simondanielsson and @Fangzhou-Ai for the review, and @shen-shanshan for the verified label. Implementation and description are updated.

## @simondanielsson — router selection and implementation placement

I checked the existing factory logic. For biased sigmoid routing with `renormalize=True`, changing `num_expert_group` from `1` to `None` changes the advertised routing method from `DeepSeekV3` to `MiniMax2`, so the current `routing_method_preserved` check keeps `GroupedTopKRouter`. With `renormalize=False`, the factory already falls through.

Separately, `FusedTopKBiasRouter` still calls AITER's `biased_grouped_topk` for some supported shapes (`fused_topk_bias_router.py:258-272`), so changing the selected router alone does not necessarily eliminate the grouped op.

This explains the current dispatch, but does not rule out a refactor that preserves the routing metadata. Moving the specialization into AITER is also a valid alternative; I'm open to that placement if it is preferred.

## Auto-enabling only where it is beneficial

You were right to push on this, and the first version did not satisfy it.

The previous dispatch still allowed the fast path in eager execution whenever its shape gate passed. Interleaved `--enforce-eager` measurements on Moonlight showed a 1.8–3.5% throughput regression.

The dispatch now checks `get_forward_context().cudagraph_runtime_mode`, following the existing pattern in `deepseek_v41/amd/ops/sparse_indexer.py`. It retains AITER when the runtime mode is `NONE` or no forward context is available.

Repeating the same eager A/B comparisons after this change gave throughput differences of −0.3% to +0.5%, within the observed same-arm variation of up to 1.9%. Instrumentation observed no Triton dispatches with `--enforce-eager`, while runs with CUDA graphs enabled exercised the new path. Tests now cover the `NONE`, `PIECEWISE` and `FULL` mode checks, plus the missing-context fallback.

## Requested cleanups

The new environment variable is removed, the original `_use_sigmoid_bias_topk` helper is removed, the scoring-function check is part of the gate, the kernel is renamed to `sigmoid_single_group_topk`, and the tests add prime/odd shapes and a parametrized gate test — 62 passing cases in the targeted suite.

I also aligned the bias dtype conversion with the existing AITER wrapper and added regression coverage: `rocm_aiter_ops.biased_grouped_topk` casts `correction_bias` to the gating dtype, and without the same cast a bf16 gating output next to an fp32 bias is scored at a precision the replaced path never uses. Removing the cast fails 4 of the 6 cases in that test; the other two shapes happen not to be sensitive to the bias precision.

## Performance and accuracy

The routing microbenchmark shows 1.67–2.15× on gfx942 under CUDA graph replay, over 256/384 experts, bf16/fp32, 1–128 tokens. That is the measured range, not a claim about the whole accepted range.

I am not claiming an end-to-end speedup. The initial sequential A/B result did not reproduce under interleaved testing and has been withdrawn. Interleaved results on Moonlight and Kimi-VL are +0.4%–0.8%, comparable to the observed same-arm variation.

The requested 8k/1k and 64k/1k points remain incomplete. Kimi-VL has a 131072 context, so the window is not the obstacle, but both the AITER baseline and this PR encounter the same HSA exception in the current test environment; the root cause has not been isolated.

The three reported NIAH task scores match between arms, although the subtask scoring zero on both arms is inconclusive. Across three interleaved GPQA runs per arm, the difference changes sign. These tests do not show a consistent accuracy change, but are insufficient to establish accuracy equivalence.

For the routing comparison, all selected expert ids match in 3323/3328 calls on Moonlight and 1248/1248 calls on Kimi-VL. The five differing Moonlight calls are reported in the PR description.

One validation limitation: the e2e and accuracy comparisons used the same older container vLLM build for both arms because of AITER compatibility issues. Unit and microbenchmark results were obtained against `db3b0f0fa`.

## @Fangzhou-Ai — parameter bounds

The gate uses shape limits rather than model names, and correctness coverage now includes Moonlight, Kimi-K2 and synthetic prime/odd shapes. However, the current measurements do not establish that these thresholds or the single-wave configuration are optimal across the entire accepted range.

`_MAX_TOKENS=128` selects small batches, primarily covering decode and speculative verification; it does not distinguish execution phases, and a short prefill can satisfy it. The larger prefill batches observed in the live run fell back to AITER. Performance evidence is currently limited to the listed configurations on gfx942.

You were right to push on this. I checked, and it changed where the patch belongs — the PR is respun accordingly.

## What blocks the factory change today

The advertised routing method is not a label. `layer.py:378` takes it from `router.kernel_routing_method_type` and stores it on the MoE config, where the AITER mxfp4 expert kernels consume it three ways: `_supports_routing_method` lists `[Renormalize, RenormalizeNaive, DeepseekV4, DeepSeekV3]`, `self.renormalize` is derived from the same tuple, and the apply path branches on `DeepSeekV3` to pick `score_mode="sigmoid"`. `MiniMax2` is in none of them, so degenerating `num_expert_group` 1 → None would make those backends refuse these models and would flip `renormalize` to False for a checkpoint whose config says `norm_topk_prob: true`. The specific blocker is `fused_topk_bias_router.py:422`, where `routing_method_type` hardcodes `num_expert_group=None`.

## But changing the router would not remove the op

I measured this rather than reading it. Calling `fused_topk_bias` directly — the routine `FusedTopKBiasRouter` uses — with a 64-expert, top-6 sigmoid+bias router on ROCm with AITER enabled:

```
synthesised group count for 64 experts: 2
aiter fused moe enabled: True
biased_grouped_topk CALLED 1x with (num_expert_group, topk_group) = (2, 2)
```

`_aiter_get_num_expert_group` picks a divisor AITER has a kernel for, with `topk_group == num_expert_group` so the grouping is a no-op ("Grouping is a no-op here, so any divisor", lines 108-124). So a model moved off `GroupedTopKRouter` would still reach the grouped kernel, and would reach it with a fabricated two-group configuration in place of its real single group.

## What I changed

Your intuition — no grouping, no grouped work — is right; it just needs to act one level down. The specialization now sits in `rocm_aiter_ops.biased_grouped_topk`, the single call site both routers reach, and the condition is generalised from "one group" to "no group is eliminated" (`topk_group >= num_expert_group`). That covers `GroupedTopKRouter` passing the model's real `1/1` and `FusedTopKBiasRouter` passing a synthesised `2/2`, needs no routing-metadata change, and leaves router selection alone.

`rocm_aiter_moe.py` is no longer modified at all. The diff is three files, additions only.

New coverage for the generalised condition:

- `test_flat_topk_matches_aiter_with_uneliminating_groups` — `num_expert_group == topk_group` ∈ {1, 2, 4, 8} × renormalize on/off, each compared against AITER.
- `test_biased_grouped_topk_substitutes_only_when_expected` — the wrapper substitutes for `1/1` and `2/2` under a graph, and does not for `8/4` (a group is eliminated) or in eager.

72 passing cases in the targeted suite, `pre-commit` clean.

One caveat on scope: the gate no longer checks `scoring_func`. At this call site the op is AITER's biased (sigmoid) top-k by construction, so matching that op rather than the router's declared scoring function is the contract. Say the word if you would rather keep an explicit check.

Everything else from the previous round is unchanged: no env var, the CUDA-graph restriction with the eager regression numbers behind it, and no end-to-end speedup claimed.

Measurements are on the container's vLLM build, which is older than `main`; the same `fused_topk_bias_router` code is on `main` at lines 108-124 and 258-282.

Both points are resolved, and the 8k/1k and 64k/1k numbers you asked for are now in the description. No code changed in this round — the previous revision stands.

## On GPQA and Kimi-VL

Different models, so there was no contradiction: NIAH and GPQA ran on Moonlight-16B-A3B at 4096 and ~1k prompts, both far below the input length where the fault appeared. The description did not make that obvious, so Validation now opens with a table of which checkpoint carries which measurement.

## Another model that reaches this kernel

**Kimi-Linear-48B-A3B-Instruct**: `num_expert_group=1`, `topk_group=1`, sigmoid router with a `noaux_tc` correction bias, `moe_renormalize`, **256 experts / top-8**, context well beyond 64k. A probe confirms it reaches this kernel — 988 Triton dispatches at `experts=256 topk=8 grp=1/1`. 256 experts is the widest point in the microbenchmark, so it is the strongest case for the kernel rather than the weakest.

## Why the long-context runs were failing

This turned out to be a bug in the benchmark harness, not in serving, and not in this PR.

`vllm bench serve --dataset-name random` samples token ids from `tokenizer.vocab_size`. For this checkpoint that is **163842**, while the model's embedding has `config.vocab_size` = **163840** rows. Ids 163840 and 163841 therefore index past the embedding table. The dataset emits a *contiguous run* of ids, so the probability of hitting one scales with prompt length: a 65536-token prompt covers 40% of the vocabulary and nearly always includes one, an 8192-token prompt covers 5%.

That is exactly the behaviour we saw. On **stock vLLM, with no part of this PR installed**, the identical 8192-token configuration gives:

| seed | completed (3 reps) | `Memory access fault` |
|---|---|---|
| 7 | 8, 8, 8 | 0 |
| 1234 | 0, 0, 0 | 1 |

It also explains the earlier fault on a different machine with Kimi-VL, where the HSA exception named `at::native::vectorized_gather_kernel` — the embedding gather.

Replacing the synthesised prompts with real text (a custom dataset whose maximum token id is 138177, asserted below the embedding size) removes it completely: **8 of 8 runs complete at 64k with zero faults**.

Happy to open a separate issue for the harness side of this if it is useful — the fix would be to clamp the sampled ids to the model's `config.vocab_size` rather than the tokenizer's.

## The numbers

Interleaved B-A-B-A, one server per block, on Kimi-Linear:

| in / out | concurrency | AITER tok/s | this PR tok/s | Δ throughput | Δ TPOT | same-arm drift |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| 8192 / 1024 | 4 | 4305.4 | 4466.3 | +3.7% | −4.0% | 4.1% / 1.7% |
| 8192 / 1024 | 8 | 6154.7 | 6162.5 | +0.1% | −1.2% | 1.4% / 1.8% |
| 65536 / 1024 | 1 | 13528.3 | 14305.7 | +5.7% | −7.0% | 8.6% / 8.4% |
| 65536 / 1024 | 2 | 18045.6 | 17927.5 | −0.7% | −1.6% | 1.7% / 0.9% |

Every point has a same-arm drift the size of the difference between arms, so this does not change the conclusion: **no end-to-end speedup is claimed**. The 64k rows carry only 2 and 4 requests per run, which is why their drift is the largest here.

GPQA on the same model, three interleaved runs per arm: AITER 0.3889 / 0.3990 / 0.3990, this PR 0.4040 / 0.4192 / 0.4091. This PR is nominally higher in all three, by 1.0 point — I am not claiming that as an improvement, since 1.0 point is 2 questions out of 198, inside the ±3.4 point standard error, and a routing difference confined to 0.15% of calls has no mechanism to make a model more accurate. No regression; equivalence not established either.

## Where that leaves the PR

The measurable effect remains what it was: the routing op is 1.67×–2.15× faster on gfx942 under CUDA graph replay, eager is excluded by the dispatch because it measured slower, and end to end is inside the noise on three models and four input lengths. That is the same basis on which #58354 landed, with its own "no end-to-end speedup is claimed", so I would rather state it plainly than stretch it.

@simondanielsson on whether this is worth adding without a perf benefit: there is one now, and the reason it was missing before was a bug in this PR.

**The bug.** The substitution only runs while a CUDA graph is being captured, and it detected that with `get_forward_context().cudagraph_runtime_mode`. The V2 model runner captures FULL graphs with that mode set to `NONE` (`vllm/v1/worker/gpu/cudagraph_utils.py`), so on current `main` the new path never ran in a FULL decode graph. A probe on MI355X counted 0 of 2912 routing decisions substituted for Kimi-Linear-48B-A3B, which runs `FULL_DECODE_ONLY`. e678ad2a switches the check to `torch.cuda.is_current_stream_capturing()`, as `custom_all_reduce.py` and `sparse_attn_indexer.py` already do: 494 of 2912 then substitute (every captured decode size up to 128 tokens, in every MoE layer), still none in eager mode. The wiring test now captures a real CUDA graph instead of faking the forward context.

**End to end after the fix**, MI355X, `main` 3966924d, interleaved PR / base / PR / base where the base arm is the same tree with the substitution turned off:

| model | concurrency | Δ output throughput | Δ median TPOT | runs overlap? |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| Moonlight-16B-A3B | 1 | **+3.47%** | −3.42% | no: PR 261.3–262.3 tok/s, base 250.7–255.4 |
| Moonlight-16B-A3B | 16 | **+1.19%** | −1.18% | no: PR 2405–2424, base 2341–2394 |
| Moonlight-16B-A3B | 4 / 8 | −0.09% / +0.75% | −0.31% / −0.69% | yes |
| Kimi-Linear-48B-A3B | 8 / 32 / 64 | +0.01% / −0.33% / +0.19% | | yes |

The gain is where the router is the largest share of a decode step: 64 experts, where the op is 1.57x faster, and small batches. Kimi-Linear (256 experts, 1.27x on the op, linear-attention layers) is neutral. Full tables and method are in the description.

**Also changed**, following @Fangzhou-Ai's question on the bounds: the gate now stops at 512 experts / top-8 (93555417), because at top-16 rows with exactly tied scores make some launches slower than AITER. Details in the reply on that thread.

`tests/kernels/moe/test_rocm_aiter_topk.py -k "flat_topk or substitutes"`: 61 passed on MI355X with all three commits on `main` 3966924d.

@tjtanaa @shen-shanshan happy to hear your view on whether this is worth taking now.

@simondanielsson done: the description now has a five-model sweep on MI355X with current `main` (3966924d), short and long context, plus GSM8K on the two largest models. Same method as before: interleaved PR / base / PR / base, the base arm being the same tree with the substitution turned off, real-text prompts, four runs per point.

Each model was probed first to confirm it actually takes the new path while capturing graphs, since that was the bug last time.

| model | experts / top-k | TP | 1k, c1 | 1k, c8 | 1k, c32 | 8k, c1 | 8k, c8 | 32k, c1 | 32k, c4 |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Moonlight-16B-A3B | 64 / 6 | 1 | **+2.62%** | +0.73% | +0.16% | **+2.23%** (6k) | +0.26% (6k) | – | – |
| Kimi-Linear-48B-A3B | 256 / 8 | 1 | +1.34% | +0.47% | -0.00% | **+1.49%** | +0.51% | **+1.34%** | +0.28% |
| MiniMax-M3.1-Flash | 128 / 4 (4/4 synthesised) | 2 | **+1.34%** | **+0.85%** | +0.21% | **+1.29%** | **+0.65%** | **+0.99%** | -0.21% |
| GLM-5.3-Flash | 288 / 8 | 2 | **+4.17%** | +0.22% | +0.61% | **+1.15%** | +0.56% | **+1.04%** | +0.49% |
| Kimi-K2.6 | 384 / 8 | 4 | **+0.36%** | -0.21% | -0.03% | **+0.39%** | **+0.26%** | **+0.36%** | +0.14% |

Output-throughput change, 1024 output tokens; bold where no base run overlaps the PR runs. Single-request decode improves on every model at every context length; at higher concurrency the router is a smaller share of the step and the difference falls into the noise. The four negative points are -0.21% at most and all overlap. Moonlight's context is 8k, so its long point is 6k.

GSM8K (lm-eval, 1319 questions, 5-shot, greedy): GLM-5.3-Flash 92.12% → 92.04%, Kimi-K2.6 93.48% → 93.71%, both within the standard error.

Models whose grouping does eliminate experts (DeepSeek-V3/R1, 8 groups / top-4) are unchanged: the gate requires `topk_group >= num_expert_group`, and `test_biased_grouped_topk_substitutes_only_when_expected` covers the `8/4` case.

Seems like a clear perf improvement at conc 1.

Should we be on the safe side and just enable this for conc 1 then? (set _MAX_TOKENS = 1). That would significantly limit the blast radius of this

Agreed, done in 7c6559d9: `_MAX_TOKENS = 1`, so the substitution only happens for single-token batches (one request decoding, no speculation) and everything else keeps AITER. The wiring test now uses one row.

Checked on MI355X with that commit on `main` 3966924d:
- `tests/kernels/moe/test_rocm_aiter_topk.py -k "flat_topk or substitutes"`: 61 passed.
- A Moonlight-16B-A3B server substitutes 78 of the 8190 routing decisions it makes while capturing graphs, all of them in the 1-token graphs (26 MoE layers x 3 capture passes); every other captured size keeps AITER.

The concurrency-1 rows of the sweep are exactly this path, so the +0.4% to +4.2% there carries over unchanged. The description now says the scope is single-token batches and marks the higher-concurrency rows as measured with the earlier bound.

@shen-shanshan @Fangzhou-Ai this is ready for another look. Since the last round:

- Fixed a bug that kept the substitution out of FULL CUDA graphs under the V2 model runner (e678ad2a), and tightened the shape bounds to where the kernel beats AITER, 512 experts / top-8 (93555417), which answers the question on whether the bounds were derived from Kimi-K3.
